title: How to Add an AI Scribe to Jane App EHR in 2026
summary: Jane's native AI Scribe covers SOAP notes at low cost—but not claims across providers. See how a workforce platform handles multidisciplinary clinic billing.
body_text: You run on Jane App, the allied-health practice-management and EMR platform, whether you are a solo physiotherapist, chiropractor, or massage therapist, or a multidisciplinary clinic billing insurance across many provider types. Documentation weighs on all of it. Physicians spend close to two hours on the EHR and deskwork for every hour of direct patient care [1], and clinicians across settings log about 86 minutes of nightly "pajama time" finishing charts [2]. Here is the fact worth knowing up front: Jane already ships its own native AI Scribe. So the real decision is no longer whether to add a scribe. It is whether the native scribe covers everything you need, or whether clean claims across a multidisciplinary clinic and the other systems you run need more. This guide covers that honestly. Key Takeaway Jane App already has a native AI Scribe, built in-house to draft SOAP notes into the chart at low cost, so for allied-health documentation it covers a lot, especially for solo and small practices. Where it stops is clean claims across a multidisciplinary clinic and coverage across other systems. A clinical workforce platform adds that. Sully.ai integrates with Jane and adds an AI Coder that submits clean claims, plus intake and follow-up, across Jane and more than 20 other EHRs. What an AI Scribe Adds to the Jane App Workflow An AI scribe listens to the appointment and turns the conversation into a structured note. The practitioner stays present with the patient. The scribe drafts the note in seconds, and the practitioner reviews it instead of typing it. Jane's users span two kinds of work: cash-pay wellness like massage and some mental health, and insurance-billed care like physiotherapy and chiropractic. The numbers below are the burden a scribe is meant to remove. The difference on Jane is that a native AI Scribe already exists. So the decision shifts from "do we add a scribe" to "does the native scribe cover everything, or do clean claims across providers, and the other systems we run, need more." Ambient Documentation Versus Manual Charting The old flow is typing SOAP notes in Jane after each appointment. Either way the practitioner is still doing data entry. The ambient flow is listen, draft, review, sign, and ambient scribes have cut documentation time in multi-site studies [8]. The split that matters here is payer mix: massage and wellness are often cash-pay, while physiotherapy and chiropractic are insurance-billed and coding-sensitive, so on that side the note has to feed a clean claim. Jane Ships Its Own AI Scribe, So the Question Is Claims and Scale Jane offers a native AI Scribe, built in-house, that listens ambiently and drafts SOAP or progress notes into the chart. It is HIPAA and PIPEDA compliant and offered as a low-cost add-on at about $15 per practitioner per month with a free tier [3][4]. That is a strong allied-health-native tool, and Jane also owns scheduling, booking, and billing. So the decision is not native versus nothing. It is whether clean claims across a multidisciplinary clinic, and coverage across other systems, needs more than a documentation scribe is built for. That framing drives the rest of this guide. How AI Scribes Connect to Jane App There are three routes: Jane's native AI Scribe, a third-party scribe, or a clinical workforce platform. The depth decides how much of the work around the note a tool removes. The key distinction: documenting the visit and submitting insurance claims across a multidisciplinary clinic are different jobs, and a scribe only does the first. Integration type Documents the visit Beyond the note Insurance claims, across providers EHR reach Native (Jane AI Scribe) Yes, in-workflow Native scheduling and billing No claim submission Jane only Third-party scribe Yes None No Jane or many EHRs Clinical workforce platform Yes Claims, intake, follow-up Yes, submits claims Jane plus 20 more The Native Option, Jane AI Scribe Jane's own AI documents the visit with a scribe built in-house, listening ambiently and drafting SOAP notes into the Jane chart. It is HIPAA and PIPEDA compliant, low-cost, and saves 2 to 5 hours per week, and Jane also owns scheduling, booking, and billing [3][4]. This is a strong allied-health-native fit, with nothing to integrate. The honest limit is scope: the scribe documents, and it is not a coder that submits insurance claims across a multidisciplinary clinic. Third-Party Scribes Freed and S10.ai market AI scribes for Jane, and Upheal is a therapy-focused option often compared with Jane for mental-health practices [5][6][7]. These document well. The tradeoff is that they are documentation tools, and they stop at the note. Clinical Workforce Platforms The broadest tier. A clinical workforce platform integrates with Jane and adds agents across the visit and the work around it. Sully.ai integrates with Jane once, and then its agents share that connection: the AI Scribe documents, the AI Coder submits clean claims, the AI Receptionist supports scheduling and rebooking, and the AI Triage Nurse runs intake and follow-up. This is the option that adds claim submission across provider types and coverage across systems. How to Add an AI Scribe to Jane App Step by Step Five steps take you from decision to a validated note in the chart. 1. Confirm Your Jane Setup and Payer Mix Confirm your Jane setup, whether you have enabled the native AI Scribe, your disciplines, and your payer mix, cash-pay wellness versus insurance-billed physiotherapy and chiropractic. Decide what you want: SOAP documentation, which the native scribe may already cover, or clean claims across providers plus intake and follow-up, which points to a clinical workforce platform. That payer mix determines the route. 2. Choose Your Integration Method Map the methods to that goal. The native scribe gives you an in-workflow SOAP note. A third-party scribe documents. A clinical workforce platform handles documentation, clean claims, and intake through one integration. The decision rule: if you are a solo or small allied-health practice, the native AI Scribe gets you there. If you bill insurance across a multidisciplinary clinic or run more than one system, you need a clinical workforce platform. 3. Connect the Scribe For the native option, enable the AI Scribe in Jane [3]. For a third-party or workforce tool, have the vendor integrate with your Jane environment [5][6]. Whichever route you pick, two things are non-negotiable before any session audio is recorded: a signed BAA and HIPAA-compliant data handling, plus client consent for recording. 4. Map Notes and Coding to Jane Configure how SOAP notes land in the right Jane fields, and for physiotherapy and chiropractic how codes attach. The native scribe documents; a clinical workforce platform writes coded, claim-ready data and submits it. Verify it on an insurance-billed physio or chiro visit, not just a cash-pay wellness session, since that is where coding and claims actually matter. 5. Pilot Across Disciplines, Measure, and Scale Pilot across a cash-pay wellness session and an insurance-billed physio or chiro visit, since they end differently. The insurance visit is the one that reveals whether coding and claims hold up. Confirm notes land correctly, measure the time saved [3], and on the insurance side measure whether claims come out clean. Validate consent and governance before a clinic-wide rollout. What to Look For in a Jane App AI Scribe Four criteria separate the options on the shortlist. Allied-Health Fit Versus Claims Across Providers Jane's native AI Scribe is built for allied-health SOAP notes at low cost [3]. The question is whether you also need clean claims across a multidisciplinary clinic and intake and follow-up at scale, which the native scribe is not built for. Match the tool to your disciplines and payer mix, not just the single visit. Clean Claims for Physio and Chiro Physiotherapy and chiropractic are insurance-billed and coding-sensitive, and a multidisciplinary clinic bills across provider types. A scribe documents; submitting the claim is a separate job. This is where a busy clinic wins or loses revenue. Sully's AI Coder extracts every ICD-10 and CPT code and submits clean claims through one integration. Coverage Across Locations and Systems Multi-location and mixed clinics often run Jane plus other systems. Native tools cover only Jane. A workforce platform that integrates with Jane and more than 20 other EHRs covers them all through one approach. Weigh coverage against the systems you actually run. Security, Consent, and HIPAA Compliance The non-negotiables: HIPAA compliance , a signed BAA, encryption and de-identified PHI handling , MFA, SSO, role-based access, and clear retention controls. Add client consent for recording sessions. Ask where audio is processed, how long it is retained, and who can access transcripts before the pilot starts. Best AI Scribes for Jane App Five options worth shortlisting. Jane has a strong native AI Scribe, so it earns a place on the list, credited for what it does. 1. Sully.ai Sully.ai starts as a strong ambient scribe and extends into a coordinated AI workforce that integrates with Jane through a single integration. The AI Scribe documents the visit, then the AI Coder submits clean claims across provider types, the AI Receptionist supports scheduling and rebooking, and the AI Triage Nurse runs intake and follow-up. Against a low-cost allied-health-native scribe, the honest differentiators are specific. First, it submits clean claims across a multidisciplinary clinic, which a documentation scribe is not built to do, and where a busy clinic wins or loses revenue. Second, it adds intake and follow-up at scale, rebooking care plans and reactivation. Third, it covers Jane plus Epic, Cerner, Meditech, Athenahealth, and more than 20 other EHRs, which matters for multi-location groups, across 5,000+ providers and 50M+ hours of AI work delivered. Each AI role costs 80 to 90% less than the equivalent human role. Best fit: multidisciplinary and multi-location clinics on Jane that bill insurance or run more than one system. 2. Jane native AI Scribe Jane's own AI: a native ambient scribe built in-house that drafts SOAP notes into the chart, HIPAA and PIPEDA compliant and low-cost, alongside Jane's native scheduling, booking, and billing [3][4]. Standout: allied-health-native documentation at low cost with nothing to integrate. Best fit: solo and small practices that want fast SOAP notes inside Jane and do not need claim submission across providers. The honest limit is scope: it documents. 3. Freed A popular lightweight ambient scribe that markets an option for Jane and pushes chart-ready notes into the EHR [5]. Standout: clinician-loved and low-friction. Best fit: small practices that want a simple scribe, after confirming Jane fit. 4. S10.ai A cross-EHR ambient scribe that markets a progress-note taker for Jane [6]. Standout: broad EHR support. Best fit: practices wanting a cross-EHR scribe, after confirming Jane fit. 5. Upheal A therapy-focused AI EHR and scribe, often compared with Jane for mental-health practices [7]. Standout: behavioral-health depth. Best fit: therapy practices, after confirming Jane fit. Move From a Single Scribe to a Full AI Workforce Jane already documents the visit natively with its AI Scribe at low cost, which is genuinely strong for allied health. But a multidisciplinary clinic is a different scale of problem. A clinic bills insurance across physiotherapy, chiropractic, and more, and coding into a clean claim plus intake and follow-up is a different job a documentation scribe is not built for. The average hospital already runs on about 800 different software tools, and point-solution AI just adds more silos instead of a workforce. Sully takes the connected path. One integration with Jane, then a team of AI employees, the AI Scribe, the AI Coder, the AI Receptionist, and the AI Triage Nurse, sharing context across the visit. The Scribe writes the note, the AI Coder extracts every ICD-10 and CPT code and submits a clean claim across providers, and the AI Receptionist handles rebooking while the AI Triage Nurse runs intake, across Jane and any other system the clinic runs. Each AI role costs 80 to 90% less than the equivalent human role, proven across 5,000+ providers and 50M+ hours of AI work. If you are weighing an AI scribe for Jane, it is worth seeing what the full team looks like in action. FAQ Q: What is a Jane App AI scribe? A Jane App AI scribe is an ambient documentation tool that listens to the appointment and drafts a SOAP or progress note into the Jane chart, so the practitioner reviews and signs instead of typing. Jane offers a native AI Scribe, and platforms like Sully.ai integrate with Jane to add clean claim submission across provider types and intake and follow-up on top of documentation. Q: Does Jane App have its own AI scribe? Yes. Jane ships a native AI Scribe, built in-house, that drafts SOAP notes into the chart, HIPAA and PIPEDA compliant, as a low-cost add-on that saves 2 to 5 hours per week [3][4]. It documents allied-health visits well. It does not submit insurance claims across a multidisciplinary clinic or run intake at scale, which is where a clinical workforce platform adds value. Q: How do I add an AI scribe to Jane App? Decide whether the native scribe covers your needs or claims and scale need more. For SOAP documentation, enable the native AI Scribe [3]. For clean claims across providers and intake and follow-up, integrate a clinical workforce platform such as Sully.ai, confirm your Jane setup and payer mix, and pilot on an insurance-billed visit before scaling. Q: Does a Jane App AI scribe handle insurance claims and coding? Jane's native AI Scribe documents, and Jane has its own billing features, but the scribe is built for SOAP notes, not clean claim submission across a multidisciplinary clinic [3]. For physiotherapy and chiropractic billing across provider types, you need coding-to-claim, which a clinical workforce platform provides. Sully.ai's AI Coder extracts every ICD-10 and CPT code and submits clean claims through one integration with Jane. Q: Should we use the native Jane scribe or add a platform? Use the native AI Scribe if you are a solo or small allied-health practice that wants fast SOAP notes inside Jane at low cost [3]. Add a clinical workforce platform if you are a multidisciplinary clinic billing insurance or running more than one system. Sully.ai integrates with Jane and adds clean claims and intake across providers. title: The best People Data Labs alternatives in 2026
summary: The best People Data Labs alternatives in 2026, compared on data access, API depth, pricing, and how much of the outbound job each tool runs.
body_text: The best People Data Labs alternative depends on whether you want raw data through an application programming interface (API) or an outcome. If you want records to build with, Clay and ZoomInfo are closest. If you want the data plus an AI that runs the outreach, Artisan is the pick: over 250M B2B professionals, waterfall enrichment, and an AI business development representative (BDR) that books meetings. People Data Labs (PDL) is an API-first data company. It ships person and company datasets through developer endpoints so teams can embed enrichment into their own products and pipelines. This composability is its whole reason to exist, and for engineering-led teams it is useful. But an API is not an outbound motion. Most teams evaluating PDL are choosing between building on raw data and buying something that already turns data into meetings, and the right alternative sits on one side of this line or the other. How the best People Data Labs alternatives compare Rank Tool Best for Standout capability Public pricing 1 Artisan Data plus an AI that runs outreach Autonomous AI BDR on over 250M B2B professionals Usage-based credits for Ava's work; dialer seats billed separately; free trial ( see pricing ) 2 Clay Orchestrating raw data yourself Over 150 enrichment providers, Claygent $167-446/month public tiers 3 ZoomInfo Enterprise data depth and API GTM Intelligence Platform, WebSights Over $15K/year reported 4 Apollo Self-serve data plus sequencing All-in-one prospecting Free to $119/user/month 5 Cognism EMEA compliance and phone data Diamond Data verification About $15-50K/year reported 6 LeadIQ Fast capture into CRM One-click prospect capture Pro $200/month for up to five users Why do teams look for a People Data Labs alternative? A few reasons. Build cost comes first, since PDL gives you raw data and you supply the engineering to clean, match, and activate it, which is fine for a data team and painful for a go-to-market (GTM) team that just wants pipeline. Coverage and freshness matter too, because some teams want a provider whose match rates and recency are easier to evaluate without building test harnesses. And, most often, scope. PDL has no sequencer, no dialer, no reply handling, and no interface a rep logs into. If your goal is meetings instead of a data pipeline, an API is the long way around. So the alternative you want depends on your builder appetite. Keep building on raw data, orchestrate it with less code, or stop building and buy the motion. How we chose We weighed four criteria for a PDL evaluator. How much of the outbound job the tool runs versus how much you build. Data and signal depth, including access model. Pricing transparency. And deployment fit, from a developer embedding an API to a revenue operations (RevOps) team running outbound for a large account executive (AE) org. For the wider category, see our guide to the best B2B data providers and the best email and phone number finder tools for sales . What is the best alternative to People Data Labs overall? 1. Artisan: Data plus an AI that runs the whole motion Artisan is the alternative for teams whose actual goal is pipeline, not a data pipeline. Instead of an API you build on, Ava, the AI sales agent at its core, works a database of over 250M B2B professionals in over 200 countries, plus Artisan Local Data with over 250M local businesses, using natural-language search and ideal customer profile (ICP) filters in an interface a rep or a RevOps admin actually uses. Intent signals like funding rounds, new executive hires, and active hiring narrow the list further, and waterfall enrichment runs across roughly a dozen providers and charges only on a successful match. Then Ava does everything PDL leaves you to build. She writes one-to-one messaging, launches email, social media, and dialer sequences on each lead's local business hours, qualifies replies against a knowledge base, chases follow-ups, and books meetings with CRM-owner routing. Autonomy is a dial: review-and-approve, objections-only, or full autonomy with plain-language escalation rules and a full audit trail. Over 90% of customers run Ava autonomously. Native Salesforce and HubSpot sync means the data lands on the right record without you writing the integration. The proof is in outcomes, not endpoints. Amelia Lerutte, Chief AI Officer at SaaStr, said "Email has always been our number one driver. Artisan is now neck-and-neck in both output and closed-won revenue," after Ava sent 6,892 emails at a 3.6% positive response rate in about six weeks. For a team weighing months of engineering against a system that already books meetings, this is the trade. Best for: teams from startup to enterprise that want data and outreach in one system, without building the activation layer Who should pick something else: a product or data team that specifically needs raw data via API to embed in their own software Pricing: usage-based credits for Ava's work, so you pay for the work she performs; dialer seats and phone numbers billed separately; free trial. See pricing 2. Clay: Orchestrate raw data with less code Clay is the best alternative if you want to keep building but write less glue. It orchestrates over 150 enrichment providers, including sources like PDL, with Claygent agents on top, publishes tiers from $167 to $446 per month, and reached a $3.1B valuation in August 2025. Where PDL is one API you code against, Clay is a workbench that composes many providers with a spreadsheet-like interface. It is still infrastructure, not an engine. You, or a GTM engineer whose time runs about $160K a year, design and maintain the workflows, and median contracts land near $30K per year. Clay gives you the workbench; you still supply the worker. See Artisan vs. Clay . Best for: RevOps and GTM engineers who want to orchestrate multiple data sources without full custom code Who should pick something else: teams that want outcomes out of the box, or developers who want a single raw-data API to embed Pricing: $167-446/month public tiers; median contracts around $30K/year 3. ZoomInfo: Enterprise data depth with an API ZoomInfo is the depth alternative for teams that want a bigger, enterprise-grade dataset with API access. Now positioned as a go-to-market intelligence platform, trading as $GTM, it claims over 321M profiles (a vendor figure) and adds WebSights and Scoops. For enterprises standardizing on one deep data source with an intent layer, it is the established choice. It is heavier and pricier than PDL: entry contracts are reported at over $15K per year, gated, and the contract terms have a reputation. Execution remains an add-on, so you are still building the motion on top. Best for: enterprises that want the deepest US data, with API access, to build around Who should pick something else: budget-conscious developers, or anyone who wants the outreach run for them Pricing: over $15K per year reported, gated 4. Apollo: Self-serve data plus sequencing Apollo is the alternative for teams that want data plus a way to act on it without any engineering. It offers over 230M contacts, is used by over 600,000 companies (over 100,000 paying), publishes pricing from free to $119/user/month, and bundles sequencing and assistive AI. Where PDL needs you to build the activation, Apollo ships a usable one. The AI is assistive, the model is per-seat, and enterprises treat it as a data layer. But for a small go-to-market team that picked PDL and then realized they had no way to use the data, Apollo is a fast, cheap correction. See Artisan vs. Apollo , Apollo vs. Lusha , and Apollo vs. Outreach . Best for: SMB and mid-market teams that want data plus sequencing with no build Who should pick something else: developers who need raw API data, or teams that want an AI to own replies and booking Pricing: free to $119/user/month, per its pricing page 5. Cognism: Compliance-first EMEA data Cognism is the alternative when compliance and coverage in Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA) matter more than API flexibility. Diamond Data phone verification, do-not-call (DNC) and Telephone Preference Service (TPS) scrubbing, and GDPR-aligned processing make it the European data leader. Some teams pair it as a phone-data source where PDL's coverage is poor. Pricing is gated and reported around $15-50K per year, and it is a data provider, so activation is separate. For diligence: its Kaspr subsidiary was fined 240,000 euros by France's data protection regulator, the CNIL, in December 2024, per the regulator. Best for: EMEA teams that need compliant, verified phone data Who should pick something else: developers who want composable API data, or US-only teams Pricing: about $15-50K/year reported, gated 6. LeadIQ: Fast capture into CRM LeadIQ is the alternative for a sales team that never wanted an API in the first place, just clean contacts in their sequencer. It captures a prospect and pushes verified data into CRM and cadence tools in a few clicks. For sales development representatives (SDRs), it is the human-facing version of what a developer would call an enrichment endpoint. It is a capture layer, not an engine, so the writing, replying, and booking stay manual, and its depth is mid-range and US-centered. But as a no-code way to move contacts into a workflow, it is purpose-built. Best for: SDR teams that want fast, clean capture into their existing stack, no code Who should pick something else: developers embedding data via API, or teams that want the outreach handled Pricing: Pro $200/month for up to five users (200 credits) What is the best enterprise alternative to People Data Labs? For enterprises, the question is whether you are building a data platform or buying a go-to-market outcome. If you are building, ZoomInfo is the deepest enterprise data source with an API and an intent layer to standardize on. If you are buying the outcome, Artisan is the pick: it delivers data and activation in one governed system, with central-ops deployment where sales ops runs Ava for large AE teams who never log in, SOC 2 Type II attestation, GDPR and CCPA compliance, single sign-on (SSO), SAML, role-based access, and a full audit trail. The enterprise argument for Artisan over an API is total cost, because a raw-data API still needs the engineering, sequencer, dialer, and reply layer that Artisan includes, and typical enterprise outbound stacks run five to eight tools before headcount. Stay with People Data Labs if... PDL is the right choice for the right team. Stay with People Data Labs if you are a product or data team embedding contact and company data directly into your own software or internal pipelines, where an API is exactly the interface you want. Stay if you have the engineering to clean, match, and activate raw data and value that control. And stay if data is your product, not just your sales input. The case to switch appears when your real goal is booked meetings and you find yourself building the sequencer, dialer, and reply logic that a platform would give you out of the box. Frequently asked questions What is the best People Data Labs alternative in 2026? It depends on your goal. To keep building on raw data with less code, Clay orchestrates over 150 providers. For maximum enterprise data depth, ZoomInfo. For teams that want data plus the outreach run for them, Artisan pairs over 250M B2B professionals and waterfall enrichment with an AI BDR, and over 90% of customers run her autonomously. Is there a People Data Labs alternative that includes outreach? Yes. PDL is data-only, but Apollo bundles data with sequencing self-serve, and Artisan goes further by running the whole motion: sourcing, enrichment, personalized email, social media, and dialer outreach, reply handling, and meeting booking. If your aim is meetings instead of a data pipeline, this changes the build-versus-buy math substantially. Which alternative is best for developers who want an API? If you specifically need composable, embeddable data, PDL is well suited and Clay adds orchestration across many providers. ZoomInfo offers an enterprise API with deeper data at a higher price. Artisan is not an API-first data vendor; it is a platform where the data feeds an AI that runs outbound, aimed at teams that want the outcome instead of the raw endpoint. What is the best enterprise alternative to People Data Labs? ZoomInfo if you are building a data platform and want the deepest enterprise source, or Artisan if you want to buy the go-to-market outcome. Artisan adds central-ops deployment, SOC 2 Type II, SSO, SAML, role-based access, and a full audit trail, and folds data plus activation into one system instead of a raw API you build around. How is Artisan different from People Data Labs? PDL delivers raw data through an API for you to build on. Artisan sources leads across over 250M B2B professionals, verifies data with waterfall enrichment (charged only on success), writes messaging, runs outreach across email, social media, and dialer steps, handles replies, and books meetings. One is an ingredient; the other is the finished motion. Can I use People Data Labs data inside another platform? Yes, that is the point of an API-first provider, and orchestration tools like Clay integrate many sources including PDL-style data. Platforms like Artisan instead ship their own database of over 250M B2B professionals with waterfall enrichment built in, so you receive verified data and activation without wiring an external API into a separate execution stack. The bottom line People Data Labs is a strong API-first data company for teams building on raw data. But if your real goal is pipeline, an API means engineering the sequencer, dialer, and reply logic yourself. Artisan delivers the data and runs the motion. title: Seltz: Web Knowledge for AI Agents
summary: AI agents need real-time web context to reason effectively. Today we're highlighting Seltz, a Web Knowledge API that provides real-time, context-engineered data from the live web, now available on Orthogonal.
body_text:
Building AI agents that need access to precise, factual, and up-to-date web information? Large language models often struggle with exact figures, niche facts, and continuously changing data, relying instead on patterns learned from past exposure. Your agents need real-time, machine-ready access to web knowledge. Today we're excited to highlight Seltz , a Web Knowledge API designed from the ground up to serve AI as the primary consumer of the Web, now available on Orthogonal. What is Seltz? Seltz is a Web Knowledge API that provides real-time, context-engineered data from the live web, optimized for use in AI systems and applications. It delivers fast, up-to-date web data, providing context-engineered web content with sources for real-time AI reasoning. Seltz is designed for teams building large language model applications, RAG pipelines, and autonomous agents that require reliable and efficient access to live web knowledge. Key Features Context That Matters Context is selected, filtered, and ranked to deliver only the most relevant web signals, no irrelevant clutter. Web content is processed and shaped to maximize usefulness for LLMs, AI agents, and RAG pipelines. Fast at Scale Built for speed and scalability, with predictable latency and performance under real-world load. Designed for high-throughput environments, with predictable performance and support for enterprise deployment needs. Simple API One endpoint. Send a query, get back structured documents with URLs and full content. No complex query syntax, no parsing raw HTML. Integrate fast, source-backed web context into your system in minutes. Enterprise-Grade by Design End-to-end pipeline ownership ensures customer data remains within internal systems, without reliance on external providers. Security, availability, and confidentiality controls are designed in alignment with SOC 2 trust service principles and requirements. Using Seltz with Orthogonal Get Real-Time Web Context Unlike cached indexes or stale training data, Seltz returns live web content. Ask about something that happened today and get structured, sourced results back. // Using @orth/sdk // Install: npm install @orth/sdk import Orthogonal from "@orth/sdk" ; const orthogonal = new Orthogonal ( { apiKey : process . env . ORTHOGONAL_API_KEY , } ) ; // Get real-time information, not stale training data const result = await orthogonal . run ( { api : "seltz" , path : "/v1/search" , body : { query : "latest AI funding rounds this week" , max_results : 10 } } ) ; // Every result comes back as a structured document with source URL and full content // No parsing HTML. No short snippets. Just clean, machine-ready text. for ( const doc of result . documents ) { console . log ( doc . url ) ; // Source URL for citation and verification console . log ( doc . content ) ; // Full document content, ready for LLM context } Structured Documents, Not Links This is the key difference. Traditional search returns ranked links and short snippets. Seltz returns full document content with sources, structured for LLM consumption. // Your agent gets back structured documents it can reason over directly const result = await orthogonal . run ( { api : "seltz" , path : "/v1/search" , body : { query : "Claude Opus 4.7 capabilities and benchmarks" , max_results : 5 } } ) ; // Each document has the full content, not a 160-character snippet // Feed these directly into your LLM context window for ( const doc of result . documents ) { console . log ( ` Source: ${ doc . url } ` ) ; console . log ( ` Content length: ${ doc . content . length } chars ` ) ; console . log ( doc . content ) ; } // Use in a RAG pipeline: pass documents directly as context const context = result . documents . map ( doc => ` [Source: ${ doc . url } ]

title: Alaska Airlines adds new nonstop Portland–Steamboat Springs winter flights
summary: The Portland-Steamboat Springs route will operate Thursdays and Saturdays from Feb. 11, 2027, through March 28, 2027.
body_text: This winter, Alaska Airlines is launching new nonstop seasonal flights from Portland International Airport (PDX) to Yampa Valley Regional Airport (HDN), giving Oregon travelers an easier way to reach Steamboat Springs, Colorado, for skiing, hot springs and long-weekend winter getaways. The Portland-Steamboat Springs route will operate Thursdays and Saturdays from Feb. 11, 2027, through March 28, 2027. The seasonal nonstop service is timed for peak winter travel to Steamboat Springs, a well-known Colorado ski destination also known as Ski Town, U.S.A.®.

summary: FOSTER CITY, Calif., July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Geron Corporation (Nasdaq: GERN), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company aiming to change lives by changing the course of blood cancer, today announced that it will release its second quarter 2026 financial results and business highlights
body_text: Geron Plans to Announce Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results on August 5, 2026 July 22, 2026 PDF Version FOSTER CITY, Calif., July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Geron Corporation (Nasdaq: GERN), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company aiming to change lives by changing the course of blood cancer, today announced that it will release its second quarter 2026 financial results and business highlights before the market opens on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, via press release, which will be available on the Investors and Media section of the Company’s website. Geron will host a conference call and webcast at 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time. A live and archived audio webcast of the conference call will be available from the Investors and Media section of the Company’s website at www.geron.com . About Geron Geron is a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company aiming to change lives by changing the course of blood cancer. Our first-in-class telomerase inhibitor RYTELO® (imetelstat) is approved in the United States and the European Union for the treatment of certain adult patients with lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes with transfusion dependent anemia. We are also conducting a pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial of imetelstat in JAK-inhibitor relapsed/refractory myelofibrosis, as well as studies in other hematologic malignancies. Inhibiting telomerase activity, which is increased in malignant stem and progenitor cells in the bone marrow, aims to potentially reduce proliferation and induce death of malignant cells. To learn more, visit www.geron.com or follow us on LinkedIn . Investors and Media Dawn Schottlandt Senior Vice President, Investor Relations and Corporate Affairs dschottlandt@geron.com
